blocks.content: Docker runs its own internal DNS server on user-defined networks, automatically resolving container names to their current internal IP addresses, exactly what makes container-to-container communication by name possible.

Any custom (user-defined) network comes with Docker's built-in DNS resolution running automatically, no configuration required, every container on that network can resolve every other container's name to its IP.

blocks.alt: Built in, running automatically, no setup needed

blocks.content: This matters beyond simple convenience: if a container is removed and a new one with the same name starts up (getting a new internal IP in the process), name-based resolution transparently points at the new IP, application config referencing the container by name never has to change.

blocks.alt: A name that keeps resolving correctly, even after a restart

blocks.content: 3. A Real Gap on the Default Bridge
blocks.text: 3. A Real Gap on the Default Bridge

blocks.content: This automatic DNS resolution is specifically a custom-network feature, the default bridge network does not provide it. Containers there historically needed the now-deprecated --link flag or hardcoded IPs to reach each other by anything other than a raw IP address, one more reason custom networks are the practical default recommendation.

blocks.alt: The default bridge genuinely lacks this convenience

blocks.content: 4. This Is What Makes Compose Feel Seamless
blocks.text: 4. This Is What Makes Compose Feel Seamless

blocks.content: This is precisely the mechanism behind Docker Compose services referring to each other by their service names, covered in depth in the Docker Compose module, Compose creates a custom network for you automatically, so every service's name just works as a hostname for every other service, with zero manual DNS configuration.

blocks.alt: The exact mechanism behind Compose's service-name networking

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: Custom networks include automatic DNS resolution by container name, kept correctly up to date even as containers are recreated.
The default bridge network lacks this, one more concrete reason to prefer a custom network for any multi-container setup.
